name: Pinecone Bromeliad
description: Acanthostachys strobilacea, commonly known as Pinecone Bromeliad (or Pineapple Bromeliad), is an epiphytic bromeliad native to tropical South America (Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina). It belongs to the Bromeliaceae family and features a rosette of stiff, spiny, gray-green leaves (20-40 cm long) in a pineapple-like form. The central tank holds water and creates a mini ecosystem. It produces small, inconspicuous flowers and reaches 20-40 cm in height. In the wild it grows as an epiphyte on tree trunks and branches. In terrariums it adds natural beauty with its distinctive form and is popular among bromeliad enthusiasts.
careTips: Requires high humidity (60-80%) - ideal for terrariums
Bright indirect light is essential - avoid direct sun
Keep central rosette (tank) filled with water - this is how it absorbs moisture
Well-draining epiphytic mix recommended - orchid bark, sphagnum moss
Native to tropical South America - prefers warm, humid conditions (18-24°C)
Epiphytic nature - can be mounted on wood or grown in pots
Can be grown in terrariums, paludariums, or aereriums
Watch for scale insects and mealybugs
After flowering, plant produces offsets (pups) that can be separated
